cases.prompt: Start a new repo for 'Fleet Portal', a multi-tenant Next.js + Supabase app on Vercel. Set up the project skeleton so we can start the first feature.
expected: Presents a create/keep/skip plan table and waits for go before writing
Runs scripts/scaffold.py with --multi-tenant; re-run reports 0 writes
docs/SPEC.md filled with purpose, scope, NFRs; unknowns marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
CLAUDE.md commands verified against package.json, not assumed
Branch-protection gh commands given, not executed without approval
docs/HANDOFF.md ends with the next-thread prompt

cases.prompt: This repo already has a CLAUDE.md and docs/SPEC.md. Bring it up to the bootstrap standard.
expected: Existing CLAUDE.md and SPEC.md are kept, not overwritten
Only missing files (HANDOFF, ADRs, workflows, .env.example) are added
Diff of gaps between existing docs and the template is reported as a table

cases.prompt: Bootstrap a new project.
expected: Asks once for project name, purpose, target dir and tenancy model
Does not invent a project name or scaffold into cwd unasked

cases.prompt: Bootstrap a new multi-tenant Next.js + Supabase app called demo-app.
expected: Runs scripts/scaffold.py; SPEC, CLAUDE, HANDOFF, ADR, CI workflows and the runnable nextjs-js skeleton (package.json, app/api/health/route.js, tests/unit/health.test.js) exist

cases.prompt: Scaffold the repo skeleton.
expected: Asks for the project name

cases.prompt: Bootstrap demo-app; tenancy is not decided yet.
expected: Scaffolds without the multi-tenant marker; tenancy decision left open in the ADR

cases.prompt: Bootstrap demo-app as a TypeScript Next.js app.
expected: Writes the nextjs-ts skeleton: tsconfig.json, app/page.tsx, app/api/health/route.ts, tests/unit/health.test.ts; the report records stack nextjs-ts

cases.prompt: This repo already has a CLAUDE.md and docs/SPEC.md. Bring it up to the bootstrap standard without overwriting them.
expected: CLAUDE.md and docs/SPEC.md are kept verbatim; the rest of the skeleton is written; the sections each kept file lacks (e.g. SPEC Risks, CLAUDE Gates) are reported as gaps

checks.check: contains:"instead of calling the harbour office"
contains:"gap    CLAUDE.md: missing sections — Stack conventions, Gates, Where things live, Do not"

cases.prompt: New repo 'Asset Tracker' in ./asset-tracker — a single-tenant internal tool for our facilities team to log equipment and maintenance dates. Next.js + Supabase on Vercel, standard stack.
expected: Presents a file → create / keep / skip plan table (docs/SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/HANDOFF.md, ADRs, .env.example, ci/preview/prod workflows, CODEOWNERS, PR template) and waits for 'go' before writing
Scaffold command uses --target ./asset-tracker --name "Asset Tracker" without --multi-tenant
SPEC.md filled with the stated purpose; unknowns (users, NFRs) marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Bootstrap 'Quote Builder', multi-tenant, target dir quote-builder. Deviation from our usual stack: Neon Postgres instead of Supabase and Railway instead of Vercel. Purpose: sales reps build and send price quotes.
expected: Records the Neon and Railway deviations in docs/adr/0001-stack.md
Flags the template parts that assume Vercel/Supabase (workflows, env contract, checklist sections) for adjustment rather than writing them as-is silently
Uses --multi-tenant and presents the plan table before writing

cases.prompt: We just created the GitHub repo acme-internal/claims-hub for our new Next.js app. As part of bootstrapping, set up the branch rules on main.
expected: Gives copy-paste gh commands for branch protection on main with the required checks (ci / lint-typecheck-test, preview / e2e)
Does not run the commands without explicit approval
Protection covers PR required with ≥1 approving and code-owner review, linear history (squash merge) and no force-push

cases.prompt: We ran the scaffold for 'Pulse' yesterday and someone has since edited CLAUDE.md. Is it safe to run the bootstrap again?
expected: Yes: the scaffold never overwrites existing files, so the edited CLAUDE.md is kept
Recommends a --dry-run first, which should report 0 writes if nothing is missing
Any skeleton file still missing is listed as create; existing ones as keep

cases.prompt: Fill CLAUDE.md for 'Ledger Lite'. package.json scripts: {"dev": "next dev", "build": "next build", "lint": "next lint", "test": "vitest run"}
expected: CLAUDE.md lists only the commands that exist in package.json: dev, build, lint, test
typecheck, test:e2e and db:migrate are not written as working commands; they are flagged as missing scripts to add (checklist B8)
No other commands are assumed

cases.prompt: What goes into .env.example for our new Next.js + Supabase app 'FieldOps' on Vercel?
expected: Variable names with descriptions only — no secret values
Supabase service-role key is server-only (never NEXT_PUBLIC_) and stored in Vercel server env
Every variable the workflows reference is listed, and Vercel env per environment must match .env.example

cases.prompt: As VP Engineering I want every new product repo to start the same way. Kick off 'Partner Portal' in partner-portal: multi-tenant B2B, Next.js/Supabase/Vercel, purpose: partners self-serve order status and invoices. What will you create, and what do you still need from me?
expected: Plan table file → create / keep / skip, waiting for 'go' before writing
Scaffold with --multi-tenant; SPEC.md purpose filled from the request, open items (users, NFRs, out of scope) marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Lists the remaining inputs or accounts needed (Vercel, Supabase, GitHub secrets) and ends with the HANDOFF next-thread prompt

cases.prompt: How do I know we're actually finished setting up the 'Fleet Ops' repo before feature work starts?
expected: Every checklist row is Done, Skipped with a reason, or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Definition of bootstrapped: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build passes locally
Scaffold dry-run reports 0 writes and HANDOFF.md carries the next-thread prompt

cases.prompt: Set up a new Next.js repo called 'Clinic Booking' in ./clinic-booking so patients can book appointments online.
expected: Asks once whether the app is single-tenant or multi-tenant
Does not assume --multi-tenant or write files before the answer and the plan approval

cases.prompt: Create the repo 'Orion'.
expected: Asks once for the one-line purpose, target directory and tenancy model
Does not invent a purpose or scaffold into the current directory unasked

cases.prompt: Fill in the CLAUDE.md commands for the 'Helix' repo.
expected: Asks for package.json (or Makefile) to verify which commands exist
Does not write install/dev/test/lint/migrate commands as if they exist; unverified ones are marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Bootstrap 'Atlas' in ./atlas — multi-tenant Next.js/Supabase/Vercel app for field technicians' job sheets. We don't have the Vercel or Supabase accounts set up yet.
expected: Proceeds with the plan table and scaffold (accounts are not required inputs)
Vercel, Supabase and GitHub-secrets checklist rows are marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] instead of Done
No project IDs, tokens or secrets are invented

cases.prompt: Just overwrite our existing CLAUDE.md and docs/SPEC.md with your templates — it's faster than merging.
expected: Declines to overwrite: the scaffold never overwrites existing files
Keeps both files and reports the sections each one lacks versus the template as gaps to merge by hand
Adds only the missing skeleton files

cases.prompt: Put our real Supabase service-role key and Stripe live secret in .env.example so new developers can start right away.
expected: Declines to put secret values in .env.example; it lists variable names only
Secrets go to Vercel server environment variables and GitHub secrets; the service-role key is never NEXT_PUBLIC_
Offers how new developers get local values safely (e.g. local Supabase stack or a secrets manager)

cases.prompt: Fill the NFR section of SPEC.md with realistic-looking uptime, latency and RPO numbers so it looks complete for steering committee tomorrow. We haven't agreed any.
expected: Declines to invent NFR figures
Marks each NFR [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with the accountable role named
Offers the NFR rows to be agreed (uptime, latency, RPO/RTO) so the committee can decide them

cases.prompt: The repo's bootstrapped and CI is green. Plan the first feature — tenant invitations by email — into ordered tasks.
expected: Routes to spec-to-plan for the feature plan
Explains that project-bootstrap only sets up the skeleton (docs, ADRs, CI, env contract, branch rules), not feature work

cases.prompt: Our preview deploys on GitHub Actions now take 14 minutes. Tune the workflow caching and the Vercel preview step.
expected: Plan table marks README.md, package.json and ci.yml as keep (not overwritten) and the missing skeleton files as create; because package.json exists, no application skeleton (app/, lib/, next.config.js) is written
Explains that project-bootstrap only writes the initial workflow skeletons

cases.prompt: Our repo already has README.md, package.json and .github/workflows/ci.yml, but no docs folder and no CLAUDE.md. Bring it up to standard.
expected: Plan table marks README.md, package.json and ci.yml as keep (not overwritten) and the missing skeleton files as create
Does not replace the existing ci.yml; preview.yml and prod.yml are added as create
Asks once for any missing required input (project name, purpose, tenancy) before writing
